cluster.label: Soluble lysosomal protein NCLs
cluster.summary: NCLs caused by loss of a soluble lysosomal protein — the group where enzyme replacement is plausible in principle.

members.label: CLN2 disease
members.summary: A form of Batten disease that starts in toddlers with seizures and loss of skills. An enzyme replacement therapy is approved.

members.label: CLN5 disease
members.summary: A very rare inherited childhood brain disease that causes vision loss, seizures and loss of skills. There is no approved treatment yet.

top_phenotypes.label: Seizure
top_phenotypes.summary: Sudden bursts of abnormal electrical activity in the brain (fits).

top_mechanisms.label: Soluble lysosomal enzyme deficiency
top_mechanisms.summary: A missing enzyme that normally floats free inside the lysosome. Because it is soluble, it can sometimes be replaced with a manufactured version (enzyme replacement).

top_mechanisms.label: Lysosomal degradation (ceroid lipofuscin storage)
top_mechanisms.summary: Cells break down worn-out parts inside lysosomes. In all NCLs this recycling fails and waste (lipofuscin) builds up, especially in nerve cells.
